text: WSJ: ECB President Lagarde Personally Intervened to Block Binance from Obtaining an EU-Wide License via Greece According to The Wall Street Journal, European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde personally intervened to prevent Binance from gaining a foothold in the European Union. Binance had sought an EU-wide license through Greece's financial regulator, and Greek officials initially told the company that its application had been completed. Binance had prepared a press release describing the approval as a "major milestone," while CEO Richard Teng planned to travel to Athens for a photo with the Greek prime minister. The plan ultimately failed to proceed, with the WSJ reporting that Lagarde personally intervened in the process. Lagarde's intervention in Binance's EU license application was mainly driven by two considerations: first, she wanted to wait for the possibility that ESMA would take over EU-wide crypto license approvals; second, she was concerned that Binance's expansion could strengthen the dominance of U.S. dollar stablecoins in Europe and undermine the development of the digital euro. — link

text: Just In: SEC Approves Innovation Exemption for Tokenized U.S. Stocks to Trade via Onchain AMMs The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) announced that it has officially approved a temporary, conditional exemptive framework (the "Innovation Exemption") to allow limited pilot trading of tokenized National Market System (NMS) stocks on specific onchain platforms known as Tokenized Securities Venues (TSVs). The exemption provides temporary regulatory relief to TSVs, ensuring they are not immediately classified as "exchanges" under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 when offering tokenized equities through permissioned automated market makers (AMMs) and liquidity pools, while also establishing clear guidelines for liquidity providers deploying proprietary capital for market-making support. The SEC's Innovation Exemption sets four key conditions for Tokenized Securities Venues (TSVs): 1. Sanctions compliance: A TSV must be a U.S. person and comply with economic and trade sanctions administered and enforced by the U.S. Treasury Department's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC). 2. Permissioned access: A TSV must establish access standards and allow only eligible participants to trade tokenized NMS stocks on the venue. 3. No synthetic stocks: TSVs may only trade tokenized NMS stocks issued by or on behalf of the underlying issuer, or tokenized by an unaffiliated third party. The tokenized stock must provide holders with the same rights and privileges as the traditional security, including dividend and voting rights. 4. Issuer opt-out: Issuers must be given the opportunity to object to and prevent their securities from trading on a TSV. — link

text: This is going to sound counter productive but I've actually been taking a more relaxed approach to the market and research to increase my output/edge. One thing I've noticed is I'm very conscious of my time. Every hour that ticks by is a mental note jotted down by my brain which asks "was that hour productive", "did you achieve what you wanted to achieve", "where's the result". If I can't answer those questions confidently, then I go into a semi anxious subconscious state. I continue watching the hours pass during the day. Gc's not read, twitter not caught up on, haven't dd'd the 5 runners of the day, haven't done a write up/post which gives my analysis on the market etc. It's a horrible feeling and not only does it make you counter productive, it ruins your quality of life as you're sitting there wishing you were doing more when you could be enjoying something else. You won't find many bigger advocates for maxing out your screen time and sitting in front of your computer 16 hours a day if you genuinely want to reach your goals. However that's not something you can just jump into with quality output unless you're a freak. If I'm working then I want my work to be at 100% capacity, if im in a semi anxious state then my focus is all over the place and more importantly, I'm not enjoying what I'm doing. This causes me to miss the small details which separates the top 1% from everyone else. Since my training takes around 3 hours and is fairly extreme, it drains a lot of my energy during the morning. One of my favourite ways to get energy back is to literally lay in bed until I actually want to work. Say I come back from gym, shower, eat, rush to the computer to squeeze an extra hour in, my mind is in a foggy flight or fight state. I've found when I come back and recharge my battery, relax and get to a point where my laziness drives action, it consistently lets me reenter my work with a fresh perspective and clear mind. I do allow myself to go on my phone and check notifications and dexscreener etc, however the best method I've found is to lay/sit with my own thoughts or fall into a light sleep. Sometimes all I'll need is 20-30 mins, sometimes 2 hours. Even though the fomo of missing out on the next runner can be crippling, my goal is to have the best clarity for decisions, research and overall use with my time during the day. I'd rather have 5 hours of work where I'm fully optimised as opposed to 9 hours that are at 50%. This is the secret to living a balanced life while being a trader. There will be periods where you need to throw all your usual health protocols out the window due to the markets being so hot, but until then, you need to find hacks which let you operate with higher brain functionality. Eventually as you increase your output you naturally gain momentum. You can do difficult non crypto tasks like training, sports, dealing with IRL errands that distract/take energy away while still being fully switched on at all times. Like everything, it's a gradual build up and a muscle you need to train. Be aware of the small things that give/take energy from you. Write them down, note the specific details that you find consistency with, iterate, improve and repeat.

text: Only 290 People Worldwide Hold $100 Million or More in Crypto, Henley Says An estimated 290 people worldwide hold at least $100 million in crypto assets, according to Henley & Partners' Crypto Wealth Report 2026, which combines on-chain data, public information and wealth-model estimates. As of Aug. 31, the report estimates 135,694 crypto millionaires, including 92,272 with at least $1 million in Bitcoin, while the global crypto-holder population has reached roughly 742 million, about half of whom own Bitcoin. Henley's 2026 Crypto Adoption Index ranked Singapore No. 1 for a fourth straight year, followed by the UAE, Hong Kong, the U.S. and Switzerland. — link

text: Russia's Largest Stock Exchange MOEX to Launch Crypto Perpetual Futures on BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP and TRX Moscow Exchange (MOEX), Russia's largest stock exchange, will launch perpetual futures linked to its BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP and TRX indices on September 22. The contracts will be available only to qualified investors, quoted in U.S. dollars and settled in Russian rubles without delivery of the underlying crypto assets. MOEX said more than 72,000 qualified investors have traded its crypto-linked futures since the first products launched last summer, with cumulative trading volume exceeding RUB 600 billion. — link
